primary_sources.title: Chromium proxy support documentation
primary_sources.date: No publication/update date shown on the inspected page; current HEAD content inspected 2026-10-21 (search exposed Chromium revision 312b6bf).
primary_sources.use: Chrome HTTP proxy and SOCKSv5 defer destination-name resolution to the proxy for covered URL requests; SOCKSv4 resolves target names client-side; SOCKSv5 URL proxying covers TCP; proxy configuration may have bypass/fallback rules. It does not establish that all OS/browser DNS activity follows the proxy.

primary_sources.title: curl tool man page
primary_sources.date: No publication/update date shown on the inspected page; current man page inspected 2026-10-21.
primary_sources.use: The man page defines --socks5 as resolving the destination hostname locally and --socks5-hostname / socks5h:// as asking the proxy to resolve it. The examples in the article use a numeric loopback endpoint to isolate destination-name handling from proxy-hostname lookup.

primary_sources.title: BrowserLeaks DNS Leak Test
primary_sources.date: No page publication/update date shown; live methodology inspected 2026-10-21.
primary_sources.use: The page says it tests 50 randomly generated domain names, 25 IPv4-only and 25 IPv6-only, to determine DNS servers used by the browser for those lookups. This supports describing the results as test-specific observations rather than a device-wide packet capture.

primary_sources.title: Google Chrome Help: Manage Chrome safety and security (Computer)
primary_sources.date: No publication/update date shown on the inspected result; official help page inspected 2026-10-21.
primary_sources.use: Chrome Help says Secure DNS automatic mode may fall back to unencrypted lookup when resolution fails; selecting a custom provider changes that behavior and can result in lookup errors. Used to recommend checking the active setting and error rather than blindly disabling DoH.

primary_sources.title: Cloudflare 1.1.1.1: DNS over HTTPS
primary_sources.date: Last updated 2026-05-05, as shown on page; inspected 2026-10-21.
primary_sources.use: DoH carries DNS over HTTPS/port 443; used to distinguish transport encryption from resolver choice and proxy-route compliance.

primary_sources.title: Cloudflare Blog: Introducing DNS Resolver, 1.1.1.1 (not a joke)
primary_sources.use: The article explicitly says the 1.1.1.1 DNS resolver is served by Cloudflare's Global Anycast Network. Used to support the article's caution that a public resolver address and an IP-geolocation label do not describe every physical routing hop; publication date is kept separate from the 2026-10-21 inspection date.

primary_sources.title: Google Public DNS: DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH)
primary_sources.date: Last updated 2024-09-03 UTC, as shown on page; inspected 2026-10-21.
primary_sources.use: Second provider's official documentation describes DoH endpoints and encrypted transport between a stub resolver and recursive resolver. Used only for the transport distinction, not to imply a particular route.

primary_sources.title: RFC 1928: SOCKS Protocol Version 5
primary_sources.use: SOCKS5 protocol defines address types including domain-name form; protocol capability alone does not establish every client's DNS mode.

primary_sources.title: RFC 1929: Username/Password Authentication for SOCKS V5
primary_sources.use: Existing SOCKS5 article's authentication and transport-security boundary retained; not part of the new curl test.

primary_sources.title: Playwright BrowserType API
primary_sources.date: No publication/update date shown; current documentation inspected 2026-10-21.
primary_sources.use: launchPersistentContext accepts a userDataDir, returns the browser's only persistent context, and closing it closes its browser. The directory stores browser session data; browsers do not allow simultaneous instances with the same user data directory. The launch options document SOCKS proxy support.

primary_sources.title: Playwright Browser API
primary_sources.date: No publication/update date shown; current documentation inspected 2026-10-21.
primary_sources.use: browser.newContext creates an isolated context; official usage recommends explicitly closing the context before closing the browser. Its context options can receive a proxy.

primary_sources.title: Playwright network and proxy documentation
primary_sources.date: No publication/update date shown; current documentation inspected 2026-10-21.
primary_sources.use: Documents page traffic over HTTP(S) and SOCKSv5, with proxy configuration at browser or context scope; includes per-context configuration.

primary_sources.title: Playwright library installation
primary_sources.date: No publication/update date shown; current documentation inspected 2026-10-21.
primary_sources.use: Documents installing the Playwright library and downloading the corresponding Chromium binary with the Playwright CLI.

primary_sources.title: EasyBR Local API and automation development guide
primary_sources.date: Published 2026-08-08, as shown on page; inspected 2026-10-21.
primary_sources.use: The vendor document describes a local desktop API, custom proxy fields including proxyProtocol=socks5, opening an environment to obtain its CDP endpoint, connecting Playwright through CDP, and closing through the Local API. It was used only to distinguish integration paths; no EasyBR client or SOCKS route was run in this research.

competitor_and_problem_observations.evidence_origin: Read-only observations supplied by the root task owner, not independently measured site analytics.
observations: Around 2026-10-15, a user question described Google resolver addresses appearing in another country under SOCKS5 while HTTPS observations differed.
Recent vendor articles/tutorials around 2026-09-28 illustrate recurring proxy and DNS explanation formats. No competitor was used as a source of technical facts.
competitor_and_problem_observations.limits: These observations are not BrowserHub Search Console or analytics queries, volume, rank, CTR, traffic, or conversion data. No intent frequency is inferred.

existing_page_information_gain.prior_state: Already explained BrowserLeaks-style observations, Chrome proxy-side destination resolution, DoH, anycast and broad interpretation cautions. It did not provide a side-by-side browser/curl lookup map, isolate proxy-hostname lookup from destination lookup, or give concrete timeout/IPv6/DoH troubleshooting guidance.
existing_page_information_gain.change: Added BrowserLeaks' current 50-name methodology; a bilingual matrix separating BrowserLeaks lookups, Chrome SOCKSv5 destination names, proxy endpoint hostname resolution, curl local mode and curl proxy-side mode; concrete blank/timeout next steps; Chrome Secure DNS fallback context; and guardrails for DoH and IPv6. Added Google DoH documentation as a second provider source.

existing_page_information_gain.prior_state: Already covered protocol/client distinctions, proxy-hostname DNS, browser acceptance, auth and UDP limits. It lacked a safe reproducible command-line comparison and a clear table describing what each curl result can and cannot establish; it also had no developer integration sequence for a managed Playwright Chromium profile.
existing_page_information_gain.change: Added bilingual credential-free curl examples against a numeric local SOCKS endpoint using --socks5 versus --socks5-hostname, a result/limit table, failure-stage caveats, and a direct FAQ on why curl socks5h semantics must not be copied as Chrome's control. Then added a bilingual Playwright-managed Chromium integration procedure with explicit install prerequisites, a running local SOCKS listener, dedicated userDataDir, controlled context shutdown, per-worker directory isolation, and a nonpersistent browser.newContext alternative. It clearly distinguishes EasyBR Local API/CDP from standalone Playwright and explicitly says the material is neither an EasyBR hands-on test nor a compatibility guarantee.

validation_status: After bilingual Playwright integration parity was restored, npx eslint src/data/refreshed-guides-b.ts, npx tsc --noEmit, and JSON parsing passed. English and Chinese SOCKS5 sections each contain nine matching topical sections. No content tests, production build, live browser acceptance, EasyBR run or deployment were performed.
independent_review: Not performed in this execution pass.
